basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 26.' and it opens 'Vers. 26. Justior me est. Quia non tradidi eam Sela filio meo. Alia translatio dicit,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 26. Justior me est. Quia non tradidi eam Sela filio meo. Alia translatio dicit, Justificata est ex me, id est mei comparatione. Non enim fecit hoc | desiderio vagae libidinis, sed amore generandae prolis.
